title: Colossally Abundant Numbers and Nicolas' Second Criterion
content: Robin's criterion states that the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if \( \sigma(n) < e^{\gamma} n \log\log n \) for every \( n > 5040 \). Nicolas' second criterion, in the form given by Broughan, states that it holds if and only if \( n/\varphi(n) < e^{\gamma} \log\log n + e^{\gamma}(2 + \tau)/\sqrt{\log n} \) for every \( n \geq N_{120569} \), where \( N_{k} \) is the k-th primorial and \( \tau = 2 + \gamma - \log(4\pi) \); for \( N_{k} \) this inequality reads \( c(p_{k}) < E(p_{k}) \). Let N be a colossally abundant number, let \( q = p_{k} \) be the largest prime not exceeding the number \( \xi(N) \) associated with N by Nicolas, and write \( \Delta(N) = \log(\sigma(N)/N) - \gamma - \log\log\log N \). For \( \log q \geq 31 \) we prove unconditionally that \( 1.317/(\sqrt{q}\log^{2} q) \leq \Delta(N) - c(q) + E(q) + (2\sqrt{2} - 2 - \tau)/(\sqrt{q}\log q) \leq 3.973/(\sqrt{q}\log^{2} q) \). Consequently, the second inequality for \( N_{k} \) implies \( \Delta(N) < -0.654/(\sqrt{q}\log q) \). We also prove that the primorials are the extremal cases of the second inequality, and that if it holds for every \( N_{k} \) with \( e^{31} \leq p_{k} \leq X \), then Robin's inequality holds for every \( n > 5040 \) with \( \log n \leq X(1 - \log^{-3} X) - \log X \). A computation over the primes up to \( X = 100{,}000{,}008{,}765{,}439 \) verifies this hypothesis, so Robin's inequality holds unconditionally for \( 5040 < n \leq 10^{10^{13.6377}} \). To the author's knowledge, this is the largest range for which Robin's inequality has been verified: it extends the range \( 5040 < n \leq 10^{10^{13.11485}} \) of Morrill and Platt.
